fr: Je me lève à sept heures.
en: I get up at seven o'clock.
ipa: /ʒə mə lɛv a sɛt‿œʁ/
notes: The liaison between 'sept' and 'heures' turns the final t into a pronounced sound linking to the vowel.

fr: Il se lave les mains avant le repas.
en: He washes his hands before the meal.
ipa: /il sə lav le mɛ̃ avɑ̃ lə ʁəpa/
notes: The nasal vowel in 'mains' is spelled with -ains but sounds like a single nasal vowel.

fr: Nous prenons le petit déjeuner ensemble.
en: We have breakfast together.
ipa: /nu pʁənɔ̃ lə pəti deʒøne ɑ̃sɑ̃bl/
notes: The final t in 'petit' is silent here since no liaison occurs before the consonant sound of 'déjeuner'.

fr: Elle se brosse les dents après le petit déjeuner.
en: She brushes her teeth after breakfast.
ipa: /ɛl sə bʁɔs le dɑ̃ apʁɛ lə pəti deʒøne/
notes: 'Dents' sounds identical to 'dans', so listeners must rely on context to spell it correctly.

fr: Tu prends ta douche le matin.
en: You take your shower in the morning.
ipa: /ty pʁɑ̃ ta duʃ lə matɛ̃/
notes: The final d in 'prends' is silent, which can tempt learners to drop the letter entirely when writing.

fr: Nous allons à l'école à huit heures.
en: We go to school at eight o'clock.
ipa: /nu zalɔ̃ a lekɔl a ɥit‿œʁ/
notes: The liaison in 'huit heures' pronounces the t of 'huit' before the vowel of 'heures'.

fr: Je bois un café avant de partir.
en: I drink a coffee before leaving.
ipa: /ʒə bwa œ̃ kafe avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ/
notes: The nasal vowel in 'un' must be written with the silent n, not just the vowel sound alone.

fr: Il met son manteau et ses chaussures.
en: He puts on his coat and his shoes.
ipa: /il mɛ sɔ̃ mɑ̃to e se ʃosyʁ/
notes: 'Ses' sounds exactly like 'ces', so spelling depends on recognizing the possessive meaning.

fr: Elle prend le bus pour aller au travail.
en: She takes the bus to go to work.
ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ lə bys puʁ ale o tʁavaj/
notes: The final d of 'prend' is never pronounced, a common source of spelling slips in dictation.

fr: Nous marchons jusqu'à la gare tous les jours.
en: We walk to the station every day.
ipa: /nu maʁʃɔ̃ ʒyska la ɡaʁ tu le ʒuʁ/
notes: Before a plural noun, 'tous' is pronounced without its final s, unlike when it stands alone as a pronoun.

fr: Je déjeune à midi avec mes collègues.
en: I have lunch at noon with my colleagues.
ipa: /ʒə deʒøn a midi avɛk me kɔlɛɡ/
notes: The unstressed e in 'je' is a mute e that learners sometimes drop or add incorrectly in writing.

fr: Il travaille dans un bureau au centre-ville.
en: He works in an office downtown.
ipa: /il tʁavaj dɑ̃ zœ̃ byʁo o sɑ̃tʁəvil/
notes: The liaison between 'dans' and 'un' produces a z sound that must not be written as an extra letter.

fr: Elle rentre chez elle vers dix-huit heures.
en: She goes home around six p.m.
ipa: /ɛl ʁɑ̃tʁ ʃe ɛl vɛʁ diz‿ɥit‿œʁ/
notes: The liaison chain in 'dix-huit heures' links three sounds together and can obscure the correct spelling of each number.

fr: Nous dînons ensemble le soir.
en: We have dinner together in the evening.
ipa: /nu dinɔ̃ ɑ̃sɑ̃bl lə swaʁ/
notes: 'Ensemble' begins with a nasal vowel spelled en, easily confused with an or in when written from sound alone.

fr: Je regarde la télévision avant de dormir.
en: I watch television before sleeping.
ipa: /ʒə ʁəɡaʁd la televizjɔ̃ avɑ̃ də dɔʁmiʁ/
notes: The mute e in 'regarde' is rarely pronounced but must still appear in the spelling.

fr: Il se couche tôt pendant la semaine.
en: He goes to bed early during the week.
ipa: /il sə kuʃ to pɑ̃dɑ̃ la səmɛn/
notes: The final t in 'tôt' is completely silent, so learners must remember it exists only in writing.

fr: Elle éteint la lumière avant de s'endormir.
en: She turns off the light before falling asleep.
ipa: /ɛl etɛ̃ la lymjɛʁ avɑ̃ də sɑ̃dɔʁmiʁ/
notes: 'Éteint' ends in a nasal vowel sound that is spelled -eint, not with a simple n.

fr: Nous nous levons tôt le week-end aussi.
en: We get up early on weekends too.
ipa: /nu nu ləvɔ̃ to lə wikɛnd osi/
notes: The two consecutive 'nous' before a reflexive verb are easy to merge into one when writing quickly.

fr: Tu ranges ta chambre chaque matin.
en: You tidy your room every morning.
ipa: /ty ʁɑ̃ʒ ta ʃɑ̃bʁ ʃak matɛ̃/
notes: Both 'ranges' and 'chambre' contain the nasal vowel spelled an, which can be mistaken for en.

fr: Je prépare le déjeuner pour les enfants.
en: I prepare lunch for the children.
ipa: /ʒə pʁepaʁ lə deʒøne puʁ le zɑ̃fɑ̃/
notes: The liaison in 'les enfants' adds a z sound between the words that is not written as a separate letter.

fr: Il boit son café sans sucre.
en: He drinks his coffee without sugar.
ipa: /il bwa sɔ̃ kafe sɑ̃ sykʁ/
notes: 'Sans' sounds like 'cent' and 'sang', so only context tells the writer which spelling to use.

fr: Elle part au travail à pied.
en: She leaves for work on foot.
ipa: /ɛl paʁ o tʁavaj a pje/
notes: The final d in 'pied' is silent, a frequent trap since many other words ending in d behave the same way.

fr: Nous faisons les courses le samedi matin.
en: We do the shopping on Saturday morning.
ipa: /nu fəzɔ̃ le kuʁs lə samdi matɛ̃/
notes: 'Faisons' is pronounced with a schwa sound even though it is spelled with ai, an irregular pattern to memorize.

fr: Je me douche avant de m'habiller.
en: I shower before getting dressed.
ipa: /ʒə mə duʃ avɑ̃ də mabije/
notes: The silent h in 'habiller' still triggers elision, so 'me' becomes m'habiller in writing.

fr: Il attend le bus devant chez lui.
en: He waits for the bus in front of his house.
ipa: /il atɑ̃ lə bys dəvɑ̃ ʃe lɥi/
notes: The final d in 'attend' is silent, matching the pattern of other present-tense endre verbs.

fr: Elle mange une pomme après le déjeuner.
en: She eats an apple after lunch.
ipa: /ɛl mɑ̃ʒ yn pɔm apʁɛ lə deʒøne/
notes: 'Une' must agree with the feminine noun 'pomme', not the masculine 'un', even though pomme starts with a consonant.

fr: Nous rangeons la cuisine après le dîner.
en: We tidy the kitchen after dinner.
ipa: /nu ʁɑ̃ʒɔ̃ la kɥizin apʁɛ lə dine/
notes: 'Rangeons' keeps an extra e before -ons to preserve the soft g sound, an irregular spelling rule for -ger verbs.

fr: Je sors du travail à dix-sept heures.
en: I leave work at five p.m.
ipa: /ʒə sɔʁ dy tʁavaj a diz sɛt‿œʁ/
notes: The liaison in 'dix-sept heures' pronounces the final consonants of both number words before the vowel.

fr: Il fait ses devoirs après l'école.
en: He does his homework after school.
ipa: /il fɛ se dəvwaʁ apʁɛ lekɔl/
notes: 'Ses' sounds the same as 'ces' and 'c'est', so the correct spelling depends entirely on meaning.

fr: Elle se repose un peu avant le dîner.
en: She rests a little before dinner.
ipa: /ɛl sə ʁəpoz œ̃ pø avɑ̃ lə dine/
notes: The nasal vowel in 'un' is a single sound but requires writing both the vowel and the silent n.

fr: Nous éteignons les lumières en partant.
en: We turn off the lights when leaving.
ipa: /nu etɛɲɔ̃ le lymjɛʁ ɑ̃ paʁtɑ̃/
notes: 'Éteignons' contains the gn sound spelled with ign, which is easy to misspell as in or ein.

fr: Je ferme la porte à clé le soir.
en: I lock the door at night.
ipa: /ʒə fɛʁm la pɔʁt a kle lə swaʁ/
notes: The mute e at the end of 'ferme' is silent in speech but essential in the written form.

fr: Ce matin, je me suis levé tôt pour aller courir.
en: This morning, I got up early to go running.
ipa: /sə matɛ̃ ʒə mə sɥi ləve to puʁ ale kuʁiʁ/
notes: The past participle 'levé' agrees with the reflexive subject, so a female speaker would need to add an e.

fr: Elle s'est habillée rapidement avant de sortir.
en: She got dressed quickly before going out.
ipa: /ɛl sɛ abije ʁapidmɑ̃ avɑ̃ də sɔʁtiʁ/
notes: 'Habillée' takes an extra e to agree with the feminine subject elle in this reflexive construction.

fr: Nous nous sommes réveillés en retard ce matin.
en: We woke up late this morning.
ipa: /nu nu sɔm ʁevɛje ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ sə matɛ̃/
notes: The past participle 'réveillés' takes a plural s to agree with the plural reflexive subject nous.

fr: Il a pris son petit déjeuner puis il est parti travailler.
en: He had his breakfast then he left for work.
ipa: /il a pʁi sɔ̃ pəti deʒøne pɥi il ɛ paʁti tʁavaje/
notes: 'Puis' sounds identical to 'puits', so only the sentence meaning confirms the correct spelling.

fr: Je vais me préparer avant de partir au bureau.
en: I am going to get ready before leaving for the office.
ipa: /ʒə vɛ mə pʁepaʁe avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ o byʁo/
notes: The infinitive 'préparer' ending in -er sounds just like a past participle in -é, a common futur proche trap.

fr: Elle a mangé son déjeuner, ensuite elle a fait la vaisselle.
en: She ate her lunch, then she did the dishes.
ipa: /ɛl a mɑ̃ʒe sɔ̃ deʒøne ɑ̃sɥit ɛl a fɛ la vɛsɛl/
notes: 'Ensuite' opens with the nasal vowel en, which learners often confuse with an when writing from dictation.

fr: Nous avons pris le métro puis nous avons marché jusqu'au bureau.
en: We took the metro then we walked to the office.
ipa: /nu zavɔ̃ pʁi lə metʁo pɥi nu zavɔ̃ maʁʃe ʒysko byʁo/
notes: The liaison in 'nous avons' adds a z sound that links the words but is not a separate written letter.

fr: Ils se sont couchés très tard hier soir.
en: They went to bed very late last night.
ipa: /il sə sɔ̃ kuʃe tʁɛ taʁ jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: 'Couchés' takes a plural s to agree with the plural reflexive subject ils.

fr: Après le travail, je vais faire les courses.
en: After work, I am going to do the shopping.
ipa: /apʁɛ lə tʁavaj ʒə vɛ fɛʁ le kuʁs/
notes: The final s in 'vais' is silent, following the regular pattern of first-person present-tense verb endings.

fr: Elle a oublié son sac au bureau ce matin.
en: She forgot her bag at the office this morning.
ipa: /ɛl a ublije sɔ̃ sak o byʁo sə matɛ̃/
notes: The verb form 'a' is easily confused in sound with the preposition 'à', though their spellings differ.

fr: Nous allons dîner ensemble puis regarder un film.
en: We are going to have dinner together then watch a movie.
ipa: /nu zalɔ̃ dine ɑ̃sɑ̃bl pɥi ʁəɡaʁde œ̃ film/
notes: The nasal vowel in 'un' before 'film' must be written with the silent n even though only one sound is heard.

fr: Il s'est brossé les dents avant de se coucher.
en: He brushed his teeth before going to bed.
ipa: /il sɛ bʁɔse le dɑ̃ avɑ̃ də sə kuʃe/
notes: 'Brossé' stays masculine singular here because the direct object dents follows the verb rather than preceding it.

fr: Ce soir, nous allons nous coucher plus tôt.
en: Tonight, we are going to go to bed earlier.
ipa: /sə swaʁ nu zalɔ̃ nu kuʃe ply to/
notes: The final s in 'plus' is silent in this context, unlike when plus means additionally at the end of a phrase.

fr: Elle a pris sa douche, puis elle s'est habillée pour sortir.
en: She took her shower, then she got dressed to go out.
ipa: /ɛl a pʁi sa duʃ pɥi ɛl sɛ abije puʁ sɔʁtiʁ/
notes: 'Habillée' agrees in gender with elle, adding a silent e that changes the spelling but not the sound.

fr: Nous avons fini nos devoirs avant le dîner.
en: We finished our homework before dinner.
ipa: /nu zavɔ̃ fini no dəvwaʁ avɑ̃ lə dine/
notes: The liaison in 'nous avons' produces a z sound bridging the two words in speech.

fr: Demain, je vais me lever plus tôt que d'habitude.
en: Tomorrow, I am going to get up earlier than usual.
ipa: /dəmɛ̃ ʒə vɛ mə ləve ply to kə dabityd/
notes: The silent h in 'habitude' still causes elision, turning de habitude into d'habitude in writing.

fr: Ils ont quitté la maison sans prendre de petit déjeuner.
en: They left the house without having breakfast.
ipa: /il zɔ̃ kite la mɛzɔ̃ sɑ̃ pʁɑ̃dʁ də pəti deʒøne/
notes: The liaison in 'ils ont' produces a z sound linking the pronoun to the verb.

fr: Quand j'étais petit, je me levais toujours à la même heure.
en: When I was little, I always got up at the same time.
ipa: /kɑ̃ ʒetɛ pəti ʒə mə ləvɛ tuʒuʁ a la mɛm œʁ/
notes: The imparfait ending -ais in 'levais' sounds identical to other imparfait and conditional endings, so spelling relies on tense recognition.

fr: Il faut que tu te lèves avant huit heures demain.
en: You need to get up before eight o'clock tomorrow.
ipa: /il fo kə ty tə lɛv avɑ̃ ɥit‿œʁ dəmɛ̃/
notes: The subjunctive form 'lèves' looks like the present indicative but is triggered by the expression il faut que.

fr: Ce sont ses habitudes du matin qu'elle ne change jamais.
en: These are her morning habits that she never changes.
ipa: /sə sɔ̃ se abityd dy matɛ̃ kɛl nə ʃɑ̃ʒ ʒamɛ/
notes: 'Ce' and 'se' sound alike, as do 'ses' and 'ces', so context alone determines the correct spelling in this sentence.

fr: Quelle heure est-il quand tu pars travailler le matin?
en: What time is it when you leave for work in the morning?
ipa: /kɛl œʁ ɛt il kɑ̃ ty paʁ tʁavaje lə matɛ̃/
notes: 'Quelle' sounds identical to 'quel' and to 'qu'elle', so agreement with heure must guide the spelling.

fr: Bien qu'il soit fatigué, il se lève toujours à six heures.
en: Although he is tired, he always gets up at six o'clock.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa fatiɡe il sə lɛv tuʒuʁ a si zœʁ/
notes: The subjunctive 'soit' is triggered by bien que and sounds different from the indicative est only in context.

fr: Avant, je prenais le train, mais maintenant je conduis.
en: Before, I used to take the train, but now I drive.
ipa: /avɑ̃ ʒə pʁənɛ lə tʁɛ̃ mɛ mɛ̃tnɑ̃ ʒə kɔ̃dɥi/
notes: The imparfait 'prenais' marks a past habit and must not be confused in spelling with the present tense prends.

fr: Elle se demande si elle a le temps de déjeuner avant de partir.
en: She wonders if she has time to have lunch before leaving.
ipa: /ɛl sə dəmɑ̃d si ɛl a lə tɑ̃ də deʒøne avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ/
notes: 'Temps' sounds like 'tant' and 'tend', so its spelling can only be confirmed through meaning.

fr: Il faut que nous soyons prêts avant que le bus arrive.
en: We need to be ready before the bus arrives.
ipa: /il fo kə nu swajɔ̃ pʁɛ avɑ̃ kə lə bys aʁiv/
notes: The subjunctive form 'soyons' replaces the expected sommes after the expression il faut que.

fr: Chaque matin, elle se demandait ce qu'elle allait préparer pour le dîner.
en: Every morning, she wondered what she was going to prepare for dinner.
ipa: /ʃak matɛ̃ ɛl sə dəmɑ̃dɛ sə kɛl alɛ pʁepaʁe puʁ lə dine/
notes: 'Ce' in 'ce qu'elle' is often confused with the reflexive pronoun 'se' when writing from dictation.

fr: Dès qu'il se réveille, il vérifie son téléphone.
en: As soon as he wakes up, he checks his phone.
ipa: /dɛ kil sə ʁevɛj il veʁifi sɔ̃ telefɔn/
notes: The elision in 'qu'il' merges que and il into a single written unit that must not be separated.

fr: Autrefois, nous prenions toujours le petit déjeuner ensemble avant l'école.
en: In the past, we always used to have breakfast together before school.
ipa: /otʁəfwa nu pʁənjɔ̃ tuʒuʁ lə pəti deʒøne ɑ̃sɑ̃bl avɑ̃ lekɔl/
notes: The imparfait ending -ions in 'prenions' is a distinct written form that some learners simplify to -ons by mistake.

fr: Il est important que tu te couches tôt avant un examen.
en: It is important that you go to bed early before an exam.
ipa: /il ɛ ɛ̃pɔʁtɑ̃ kə ty tə kuʃ to avɑ̃ œ̃n‿ɛɡzamɛ̃/
notes: The liaison in 'un examen' links the n sound to the vowel, while 'couches' takes the subjunctive form triggered by il est important que.

fr: Le week-end, elle se levait plus tard que pendant la semaine.
en: On weekends, she used to get up later than during the week.
ipa: /lə wikɛnd ɛl sə ləvɛ ply taʁ kə pɑ̃dɑ̃ la səmɛn/
notes: The imparfait 'levait' can be mistaken for the present tense 'lève' since both are unstressed in rapid speech.

fr: Quel que soit le jour, il suit toujours la même routine.
en: Whatever the day, he always follows the same routine.
ipa: /kɛl kə swa lə ʒuʁ il sɥi tuʒuʁ la mɛm ʁutin/
notes: 'Quel' agrees with the masculine noun jour, and 'soit' is the subjunctive form required after quel que.

fr: Nous nous sommes habitués à nous lever tôt depuis que nous avons changé de travail.
en: We have gotten used to getting up early since we changed jobs.
ipa: /nu nu sɔm zabitɥe a nu ləve to dəpɥi kə nu zavɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe də tʁavaj/
notes: The past participle 'habitués' takes a plural s to agree with the plural reflexive subject nous.

fr: Il se peut qu'elle soit déjà partie travailler.
en: It is possible that she has already left for work.
ipa: /il sə pø kɛl swa deʒa paʁti tʁavaje/
notes: The subjunctive 'soit' follows the impersonal expression il se peut que, not the indicative est.

fr: Ce n'est pas la même chose de se lever tôt en semaine et le week-end.
en: It is not the same thing to get up early on weekdays and on weekends.
ipa: /sə nɛ pa la mɛm ʃoz də sə ləve to ɑ̃ səmɛn e lə wikɛnd/
notes: 'Ce' at the start and 'se' before lever sound alike but serve completely different grammatical roles.

fr: Bien que je sois fatigué le matin, je fais toujours du sport avant le travail.
en: Although I am tired in the morning, I always do sports before work.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə ʒə swa fatiɡe lə matɛ̃ ʒə fɛ tuʒuʁ dy spɔʁ avɑ̃ lə tʁavaj/
notes: The subjunctive 'sois' after bien que replaces the expected indicative suis.

fr: Elle a changé sa routine depuis qu'elle travaille à domicile.
en: She has changed her routine since she has been working from home.
ipa: /ɛl a ʃɑ̃ʒe sa ʁutin dəpɥi kɛl tʁavaj a dɔmisil/
notes: The elision in 'qu'elle' joins que and elle into one written word before a vowel sound.

fr: Quelles que soient ses habitudes, elle arrive toujours à l'heure.
en: Whatever her habits are, she always arrives on time.
ipa: /kɛl kə swa se abityd ɛl aʁiv tuʒuʁ a lœʁ/
notes: The plural subjunctive 'soient' agrees with habitudes, and 'quelles' must match its feminine plural gender.

fr: Autrefois, il se réveillait sans réveil, mais maintenant il en a besoin.
en: In the past, he used to wake up without an alarm clock, but now he needs one.
ipa: /otʁəfwa il sə ʁevɛjɛ sɑ̃ ʁevɛj mɛ mɛ̃tnɑ̃ il ɑ̃n a bəzwɛ̃/
notes: The imparfait verb 'réveillait' and the noun 'réveil' share the same root but different endings that are easy to confuse.
